releases.body:
### Proposal cards leave the inbox when the proposal is decided

* `attention.reconcile_proposals()` — run by the watcher — closes an approval
  card once its proposal is `approved`/`claimed`/`executing`/`executed`,
  `rejected`, or no longer exists. The inbox and the proposal board can no longer
  disagree about what is still waiting, which was the root of the “nothing
  pending” reply while eleven approved proposals sat unexecuted.

### Operator asks are durable, structured messages are readable, proposals show expiry

* A room message that names the operator now creates a `room` attention item
  **even when Perun also answers**. The PerunChat page shows an “N operator asks
  for you” strip, and a new **Needs you** page (and nav entry) lists room
  mentions alongside permissions, forms, proposals and handoffs; replying there
  posts back to the exact room.
* Structured (object) room payloads render as an expandable JSON preview with a
  type/status summary and a proposal chip, instead of `[object Object]`. Object
  dedupe uses a real payload key, not `String(payload)`.
* Active proposals show their expiry in the peek, the Shared row and the chip
  tooltip. The proposal MCP tools now return `expires_at`, and the room persona
  treats `approved` (awaiting claim or execution) as pending — never “nothing
  pending” while an approved proposal has no executor.

### Manage a proposal from the chat peek, and keep the focus

* The peek card now offers the state-appropriate actions directly: **Approve &
  run / Approve only / Reject / Delete** (pending), **Run now / Withdraw /
  Delete** (approved), **Revoke claim** (claimed), **Cancel** (executing), and
  **Retry / Delete** (completed). Each action re-fetches the proposal, recolours
  the chat chip and updates the card; Retry opens the new proposal.
* The focus is encoded in the URL (`#/project/<slug>/shared/<prop_…>`) and
  re-applied on every render, poll and reload, so the row is not lost when the
  view refreshes. The Shared tab now waits for **both** cards (settings and
  proposals) before scrolling — the settings card loading above the list used to
  move the row off-screen. The gold highlight persists while the id is in the
  URL and clears when another tab is opened.

### Proposal lookup hardening

* `GET /api/proposals/{id}` now hides a hidden project's proposal unless the
  caller is in the owner workspace (or `PERUN_SHOW_HIDDEN_PROJECTS`), so a
  shared id cannot bypass the hidden-project rule.
* The chat lookup cache is capped at 200 entries and no longer caches failures:
  a transient outage, or a server still on an older build, retries instead of
  pinning a neutral chip forever. **Open in project** is disabled until the peek
  has loaded.
* Regression tests now assert that the fallback shim covers every `ChatCore`
  call and that the proposal focus runs after the card is inserted into the DOM
  (the bug that landed on the tab but never on the row).

### Chat fallback and chip font

* When `chat_core.js` is missing (a stale cache or a truncated deploy), the
  permissive shim now includes `proposalIds: () => []`. Without it
  `renderMessage` threw on exactly the degraded path the fallback exists to keep
  alive.
* The proposal chip uses the real monospace stack; `var(--mono)` was undefined,
  so the declaration was invalid.

### The exact proposal is visible and reachable

* The Shared tab now shows each proposal's `prop_…` id as a copy chip, so a chat
  reference can be matched to the exact row (and copied back into the room).
* **Open in project** now really lands on that row: the focus ran before the card
  was inserted into the DOM, so the lookup found nothing and the pending id was
  consumed. It focuses after insertion, re-renders when the Shared tab is already
  open and the card is still loading, expands the completed section, and scrolls
  and flashes the row. Chip status lookups are cached for the chat re-renders.

### Proposal references in chat are actionable

* Every `prop_…` named in a PerunChat message is now a chip coloured by its
  status (the project is in the tooltip). Clicking it opens a peek card with the
  project, status, requester, intent, targets and result; **Open in project**
  jumps to the Shared tab, expands the completed section when needed, scrolls to
  the row and flashes it. A new `GET /api/proposals/{id}` resolves a proposal
  across projects, so the operator no longer has to guess which project a chat
  mention belongs to.
* Fixed the **Approve only** confirmation: it referenced an undefined `targets`
  variable and threw before sending the approval.

### Updates refresh the global install

### Updates refresh the global install

* `perun update apply` on a git checkout now re-runs the additive global install
  (`perun install --no-index`) after the pull, so the managed `AGENTS.md` kernel,
  the slash commands and the MCP entry match the release that was just installed.
  Previously only fresh installs and installer upgrades refreshed them, leaving
  git users on old always-on rules. The step backs up before writing and is
  best-effort: a locked or read-only config logs a warning and never fails a
  successful update.

### Global kernel: search with a tool, not a shell pipeline

* The managed global `AGENTS.md` block now tells every project to search with the
  `grep` / `perun_grep` tool and never with a `Select-String` / `findstr` /
  shell-`grep` pipeline. On Windows the console rendering collapses match lines
  into columns of `1`s or ANSI noise, so a search can look empty when it matched
  and a misread costs a whole retry. The template change is applied by
  `perun install` (the global block is refreshed without touching user content).
